section_summary: This section contains the opening ten pages of the American Council on Japan’s “Japanese Policy” report. It argues that detailed occupation controls have weakened Japanese initiative and slowed recovery, then recommends greater Japanese authority, lower occupation costs, and measures to encourage foreign investment.

subfiles.title: Japanese Policy
subfiles.about: A critique of the American occupation’s controls and economic policies, with recommendations for Japanese recovery and foreign investment.
subfiles.summary: The report argues that the occupation missed an opportunity to guide Japan toward democracy because SCAP imposed detailed controls and reforms while leaving Japanese officials little responsibility. It recommends replacing those controls with high-level oversight and giving Japan more authority over economic policy, labor rules, and recovery planning. It also calls for lower occupation costs, clearer exchange and tax rules, compensation for lost foreign property, changes to Japanese business laws, and U.S. guarantees to attract private capital.
